description:
The walk's reached-callsite set is NON-MONOTONE: analyze_tail /
deliver_tail_value (jobs/semantic.rs ~:686-730, ~:908) truncate a tail chain
at a call whose ReturnType has not arrived, so callsites behind it go
unreached for a round. Two measured consequences:

1. CHURN (fz-kdt.69.2's residual): CallSite retract-and-remint of 33/12
   first-appearance excess (predicate/take_drop; recipe: causal-stream
   lifecycle rows at 84ae179b4).
2. HARD GATE for decommission/retraction machinery (fz-kdt.69.3's
   refutation): retracting an abandoned key's ReturnType ground-shifts the
   abandoning caller, whose truncated rebased walk re-abandons the cone --
   perpetual motion (4,110 completion-time cycles; 1,297 drain-time; control
   without retraction: 2).

STATUS OF THE FIX: unrecovered. The 69.2 builder measured a variant
(continue past an absent delivered value) removing the churn and improving
the inventory (214->200) -- but TWO faithful reconstructions failed to
reproduce those numbers, and a third attempt during 69.3 made the
decommission loop WORSE (10,388/10,570 cycles). Do not trust the prose
numbers; re-derive from scratch, publish the actual diff in this ticket, and
verify against BOTH consequences (churn rows AND the decommission loop in
wt/kdt693-index @ 9d65ab25e). Inventory pins re-pin downward only if the
improvement is real (lowering is safe-by-construction; verify output via
canon byte-compare + full matrix).

Under fz-kdt.74's cell model this becomes a row-content question (an
unreached edge keeps standing content; nothing retracts) -- if 74 proceeds,
this ticket may be absorbed by its stages rather than fixed standalone.
title: analyze_tail truncates at absent return evidence: hard gate for any retraction machinery
